title: Consolidate projection views, remove legacy polymorphic_fks, and add tenant-aware covering indexes
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: Remove several legacy polymorphic foreign-key patterns and redundant projection views that cause planner churn and wide table scans on tenant-heavy queries. Replace with a small set of normalized lookup tables and tenant-aware covering indexes to reduce p95 read latency on control-plane read paths (projects/list, ownership joins, and audit lookups) and to shrink index bloat while keeping online migration risk low.
comments: 2025-02-10 - Triage: Observed repeated high planner time and heap read amplification on queries joining projects -> project_refs (polymorphic). Query samples and explain plans are linked in the Confluence doc. Assigned to Lara for initial spike.

2025-02-13 - Spike complete: 3 candidate approaches evaluated: 1) Denormalize small reference columns into projection views (fast reads, expensive writes), 2) Replace polymorphic_fks with single surrogate FK table (balanced), 3) Introduce expression/partial covering indexes per tenant slice (index count grows). Recommended approach: (2) surrogate FK table + targeted covering indexes for hot routes.

2025-02-17 - Design decision: Consolidate 4 projection views into two read-optimized materialized views (tenant-scoped) and create a surrogate "project_lookup" table with foreign keys to canonical entities. Will also add covering indexes: (tenant_id, project_id, owner_id, staged_at) and (tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, live_flag) to accelerate audit/ownership queries. Documented trade-offs in design doc: small write amplification vs large read wins.

2025-02-21 - Migration plan sketched: 1) create surrogate table with nullable columns, 2) backfill in batches per tenant ordered by activity, 3) add FK constraints with NOT VALID, 4) progressively enable tighter constraints and swap queries to use new lookup table, 5) drop legacy polymorphic columns and obsolete projection views after 2 weeks of metrics baseline. Backfill window estimated 6 hours for top 10 tenants; we will throttle for lower tiers.

2025-02-24 - Implementation notes: Added new SQL helper in control-plane repo to chunk backfills (limit/offset replaced with keyset by last_updated_at). Push PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1456. Integration tests added to ensure read parity for projects/list.

2025-02-28 - Index sizing & monitoring: Created ephemeral indexes in staging to measure bloat and p99 improvements. Early numbers: projects/list p95 dropped ~42%, overall index size for the projects area increased 6% due to new covering indexes but reduced overall read IO by ~28% on simulated production trace. Saved queries and dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ctlp-proj-reads

2025-03-02 - Safety & rollback: Plan includes migration flag gate in feature flags; incremental cutover per region. Rollback steps: 1) flip query path back to projection views, 2) stop backfill workers, 3) mark new indexes/constrains as drop-ready. Will keep data for 30 days before final drop.

2025-03-04 - Code review feedback (ENG & DB): DB team requested NOT VALID FK approach and an epochs-based reindex window to avoid vacuum spikes. Addressed in latest PR update and added a low-priority follow-up to replace reindexing with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY + swap pattern for peak hours.

2025-03-04 - Next steps: Merge PR after finish of index concurrency tests on staging, schedule staged backfill on 2025-03-10 in the evening maintenance window, and run validation check comparing 2000 random rows vs old query path for parity. Post-migration monitoring: cohort error rate, p95 latency, index bloat, write TPS.
Notes: Security review not required for the schema changes but audit logging of migration events has been enabled to S3 for traceability.
sql_samples:
-- Hot read: projects list with joins that exhibited sequential scans
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT p.id, p.name, pr.owner_id FROM projects p JOIN project_refs pr ON pr.project_ref = p.ref WHERE pr.tenant_id = $1 ORDER BY p.updated_at DESC LIMIT 50;

-- Proposed covering index
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_proj_tenant_cover ON project_lookup (tenant_id, project_id, owner_id) INCLUDE (name, updated_at);

-- Backfill chunk example
INSERT INTO project_lookup (tenant_id, project_id, owner_id, created_at) SELECT tenant_id, id, owner_id, now() FROM projects WHERE updated_at > $last_cutoff ORDER BY updated_at LIMIT 1000;
